title: Introduce tenant-aware cost blueprints and compact quant presets with preview CLI
author: Sofia Alvarez
release_notes:
- Add tenant-aware cost blueprint generator (safe defaults for batching/caching)
- Add compact quantization profile library with runtime fallbacks
- New rwctl econ preview command to simulate unit-econ impact per tenant
- Observability integration: blueprint telemetry and regression hooks
description: Summary: Adds a tenant-aware 'blueprint' generator that emits recommended batching, cache, and quantization defaults per tenant profile. Includes a compact set of quantization presets (q4_0/q4_1-like variants tuned for throughput on V100/A100/Inferentia), a CLI preview command (rwctl econ preview) for estimating unit economics, and telemetry hooks so Optimize and Console can show projected cost/latency tradeoffs. Motivation: Many customers want safe, opinionated defaults that reduce inference cost without manual tuning. Existing autotuners were global; this change lets us target tenant workload shape and SLOs while retaining runtime safety fallbacks. Design/what changed: - pkg/econ/blueprint.go: core blueprint generator and policy combinator (tenant SLOs, request size distribution, preferred latency-cost tradeoff). - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/ : three compact quant profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) expressed in YAML, with metadata for runtime compatibility. - runtime/compat/fallbacks.go: deterministic compatibility checker and automatic fallback to higher-precision profile when kernel support is missing. - cmd/rwctl/econ_preview.go: CLI to load a tenant sample, apply a blueprint, and output estimated unit-econ table (tokens/second, p99 latency, cost-per-1M tokens). - observability/telemetry/blueprint_events.go: events for blueprint proposals, applied profiles, and regression signals. - docs/operational/econ-blueprints.md: operational runbook and examples for Dedicated/Private customers. - tests/*: unit and integration tests that validate blueprint generation across synthetic tenant profiles, and e2e smoke that exercises rwctl preview. Commits: - 9 commits (feature scaffolding, profile YAMLs, runtime fallback integration, CLI and tests, docs). High-level commit summary: 1) scaffold econ blueprint package; 2) add compact quant profiles and metadata; 3) implement runtime compatibility/fallback logic; 4) implement rwctl preview with sample loaders; 5) telemetry + metrics + docs; 6) add unit and integration tests; 7) fix test flakiness and add mock kernel table; 8) address reviewer feedback on race conditions; 9) final cleanup and squash. Files changed (high level): - pkg/econ/blueprint.go - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/balanced.yaml - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/conservative.yaml - pkg/econ/profiles/compact/aggressive.yaml - runtime/compat/fallbacks.go - cmd/rwctl/econ_preview.go - observability/telemetry/blueprint_events.go - docs/operational/econ-blueprints.md - tests/econ/blueprint_test.go - tests/e2e/rwctl_preview_integration_test.go - internal/telemetry/mappers.go - examples/tenant_samples/* Review conversation: - Ethan Park (reviewer): "Nice shape overall. A couple of requests: 1) make the runtime fallback deterministic for concurrent lookups, 2) add a short-circuit when tenant has explicit quant ban, and 3) add a basic perf microbenchmark to track p99 impact." - Author (Sofia): "Thanks Ethan — addressed determinism by introducing a per-model compatibilityCache and added a tenant-level explicit_quant_ban flag. Added a microbenchmark harness under tests/bench/ and wired CI to run a minimal iteration." - Maya Singh (reviewer): "We need clearer UX for rwctl preview output; add a CSV output and reduce noise for default output." - Author: "Added --format csv and compact table mode. Included an example in docs and updated integration test to assert CSV columns." - Jonas Becker (reviewer): "Telemetry events look good; ensure we don't log tenant PII. Also please add a schema version to profiles so future rollouts are safe." - Author: "Stripped PII from events and incremented profile metadata with schema_version: 'v1'." - Diffs after review: race fix in runtime/compat/fallbacks.go, added explicit_quant_ban checks in blueprint generator, CSV output flag for CLI, microbench harness, and docs update. CI: - build: passed - unit tests: passed (pkg/econ unit suite) - integration tests: passed (rwctl preview integration against mock runtime) - lint: passed (go vet/gofmt/golint) - bench-smoke: passed (quick run) Merge: Squash and merge on 2026-03-01 by Maya Singh. Post-merge actions: - Scheduled a small Canary rollout to Dedicated region us-west-2 for two tenants with low-risk traffic; monitoring configured in Console dashboard sample. - Added a telemetry alert that fires if projected cost savings exceed 35% but measured p99 degrades >10%. Backwards compatibility & safety: - No breaking API changes to public inference endpoints. The blueprint generator produces suggestions only; operators must opt-in to apply. - Runtime fallback ensures that if a compact quant profile cannot be serviced on chosen hardware, we fall back to a safe higher-precision profile at runtime. Tests & verification: - Unit coverage added for blueprint combinator logic, fallback determinism, and explicit_quant_ban path. - Integration tests cover rwctl preview end-to-end and CSV export. - Bench harness provides data for future perf regressions and is wired to CI as a minimal smoke run. Operational notes: - Docs + runbook include step-by-step for enabling tenant auto-apply, previewing changes with rwctl, and rolling out via Canary. - Recommend enabling blueprint telemetry in staging for at least one week before enabling auto-apply for a tenant. Known limitations & follow-ups: - Compact quant profiles are tuned for a subset of hardware; additional tuning needed for upcoming H100 kernels (ENG-12902). - We purposely left online autotune disabled; the generator outputs blueprints and an optional manual apply to reduce risk. - Follow-up PR planned to add a UI flow in Console to preview/approve blueprints per tenant (ENG-13044). Overall impact: This PR reduces the friction of adopting cost-savvy defaults by providing tenant-aware recommendations, safe fallbacks, and a lightweight preview experience for operators.
